battle.name: 阿根廷獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 布宜諾斯艾利斯與拉普拉塔河口
battle.brief: 一八一〇年五月二十五日，布宜諾斯艾利斯五月廣場召開公開議會，總督希德諾斯被推翻，第一執政委員會成立，拉普拉塔河口的王權就此斷裂。卡面這支一五二〇年的西班牙火繩槍，到一八一〇年只剩在克里奧羅民兵手上；王軍線列步兵早已換上燧發槍，缺口由長槍與火繩槍組成的民兵方陣補上。

kit.name: 火繩槍
kit.history: 火繩槍要點火、要瞄、要排隊。方陣把這些弱點變成了整齊的彈幕。

countries: 阿根廷獨立戰爭（一八一〇年五月二十五日至一八一八年七月九日）寫在紙上是殖民地對宗主國的戰爭，實際是同一批克里奧羅人被效忠與兵役切成兩面。革命一側：一八一〇年五月二十五日，布宜諾斯艾利斯五月廣場召開公開議會，推翻西班牙維克托總督巴塔薩爾·希德諾斯·德·西斯內羅斯，成立由科內利奧·薩阿夫德拉主持的九人第一執政委員會；內陸各省隨即響應，聖路易斯、科連特斯、薩拉多、門多薩、圖庫曼各建執政委員會，國民代表大會一八一三年在布宜諾斯艾利斯開議，一八一六年在圖庫曼宣布聯合省獨立。革命軍的骨幹是城鄉民兵：布宜諾斯艾利斯舊有的民兵行會被改組成數個志願步兵團，北方軍團由曼努埃爾·貝爾格拉諾率領，安第斯軍由何塞·德·聖馬丁統帥，班達奧里恩泰爾一帶另由何塞·赫爾瓦西奧·阿蒂加斯以利奇帕鄉野的馬兵與遊騎手組成自由民族聯盟。王黨一側：西班牙王室在布宜諾斯艾利斯的總督府與守備軍、駐蒙得維的亞的里約拉普拉塔皇家軍與「王室志願兵」團隊，以及一八一一年起由塞維利亞三人執政政府自本土派來的援軍；主力包括佩德羅·安塞爾莫·德·拉·富恩特所率的皇家步兵線列團、龍騎兵與輕騎兵，另有秘魯總督轄下派出的安第斯步兵與山中的王黨游擊隊。兩軍基層多為克里奧羅、混血與瓜拉尼血統的土生民眾，分野在效忠對象，所以這場戰爭的殘酷並非殖民者對土著，而是同鄉被陣營割開。值得留意的是雙方的基層成分高度重疊：王黨一側的「王室志願兵」與革命一側的民兵同樣出於港城行會與鄉村，分野只在效忠的印章，班達奧里恩泰爾一線更出現過整團倒戈的事例。戰爭同時是一場內河水戰與邊境騎兵戰，拉普拉塔河、烏拉圭河與巴拉那河上的小型武裝船隊，與省際邊界上來去如風的騎兵，是決定戰局走向的另外兩支力量。
countriesEn: Written on paper, the Argentine War of Independence was a colony fighting its metropolitan power; in practice it was one and the same pool of criollos cut in two by conscription and by allegiance. On the revolutionary side: on 25 May 1810 an open cabildo in the Plaza de Mayo of Buenos Aires deposed the viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros and formed the nine-man Primera Junta under Cornelio Saavedra; the inland provinces answered in turn, each raising a junta of its own — San Luis, Corrientes, Salta, Mendoza, Tucumán — while the Congress of the United Provinces first sat in Buenos Aires in 1813 and declared the independence of the United Provinces from Tucumán in 1816. The military backbone of the revolution was the town and country militia: the old guild militias of Buenos Aires were reorganised into several volunteer infantry regiments, the Army of the North was led by Manuel Belgrano, the Army of the Andes was commanded by José de San Martín, and in the Banda Oriental José Gervasio Artigas formed the League of the Free Peoples out of the mounted men and free riders of the Charrúa and Guaraní countryside. On the royalist side stood the viceregal government in Buenos Aires with its garrison, the Royal Army of the Río de la Plata holding Montevideo together with the Royal Volunteers, and, from 1811 onward, the reinforcements sent out from metropolitan Spain by the Seville triumvirate; the main body of these were the royal line infantry regiments of Pedro Anselmo de la Fuente, the dragoons and the light horse, plus the highland infantry sent down by the viceroy of Peru and the royalist guerrillas of the Andes. The rank and file on both sides were mostly criollos, mestizos and Guaraní-born locals. The line that divided them was one of allegiance, so the cruelty of this war was not colonist against native but neighbour against neighbour. It is worth noting how closely the rank and file of the two sides overlapped: the Royal Volunteers on the royalist side came from the same port guilds and countryside as the revolutionary militia, and the dividing line was nothing but the seal of allegiance; in the Banda Oriental there were even whole units that changed sides. The war was at the same time a river war on the inland waterways and a war of frontier horsemen, and the small armed boats that moved on the Río de la Plata, the Uruguay and the Paraná, together with the cavalry that came and went along the provincial borders, were two more of the forces that decided the outcome.
people: 推動這場戰爭的是兩批人馬。革命一方：曼努埃爾·貝爾格拉諾，北方軍團的建立者，一八一〇年二月在巴拉那河船上首次升起藍白二色的橫幅，同年五月率團北上攻入上秘魯，贏得薩安路易斯與埃爾波斯塔兩役，卻在一八一三年十月維爾卡普吉歐與一八一四年二月阿亞庫喬連敗，兵團幾乎全滅；何塞·德·聖馬丁自一八一二年起經營安第斯山，替北方軍團訓練新銳，一八一四年率軍越嶺南下接應阿亞庫喬的敗兵，一八一四至一八一七年間在智利取得埃爾胡恩卡爾、查卡布科與邁普三戰，終於把王軍逐出南美最南端；科內利奧·薩阿夫德拉以第一執政委員會主席之名主持開國，卻在一八一一年要求把自己的名字從議事錄上抹去；胡安·德爾卡皮奧與馬里亞諾·莫雷諾力主以人民主權重寫殖民地法，影響了後來的《一八一三年法典》與圖庫曼議會的獨立宣言；何塞·赫爾瓦西奧·阿蒂加斯在班達奧里恩泰爾組成自由民族聯盟並自任保護人，一度迫使布宜諾斯艾利斯的中央派節節退讓，後於一八一七年里維拉在「弗洛雷斯戰役」中擊敗其派系，阿蒂加斯退入巴拉圭；胡安·拉瓦列、馬丁·羅德里克斯與比森特·洛佩斯·普拉內斯先後主持政府，把戰爭推向「高原之路」的極限。王黨一方：維克托總督希德諾斯於一八一〇年五月倉促返西班牙，皇家陸軍總司令加斯帕爾·德·維戈德特退守蒙得維的亞，在班達奧里恩泰爾對抗阿蒂加斯與「聖馬爾科斯驍騎兵團」；佩德羅·安塞爾莫·德·拉·富恩特、拉法埃爾·德·馬羅托、何塞·曼努埃爾·德·戈耶內切、安東尼奧·德·金塔尼利亞與法蘭西斯科·哈維耶爾·德·埃利奧，分別主持上秘魯、智利與蒙得維的亞的防務；何塞·德·拉·卡諾瓦斯於一八一八年在利瑪向聖馬丁交出城市與軍隊。兩軍多數關鍵人物在記錄裡只是編制與命令的執行者，真正改變戰局的是決定撤退、切割與合擊的少數人。北方軍團裡還有一件值得記的事：一八一四年二月二十八日，第七線列步兵團在羅德奧・德・查西一帶拒絕向同鄉的村落進攻，該團就地瓦解；這支以克里奧羅為主的軍隊正是北方軍團的骨幹，此舉等於宣告革命軍自身的戰爭已經失去對象。卡洛斯・瑪麗亞・德・阿爾維亞爾一八一三年出任執政官，一八一五年因君主制色彩與軍隊異動而下台，說明革命陣營內部對共和與君主兩條路一直存在爭議。胡安・拉瓦列一八一五年把政府遷到烏拉圭河東岸，實際上放棄了布宜諾斯艾利斯；阿蒂加斯於一八一九年退入巴拉圭，於一八二〇年病逝。
peopleEn: Two sets of men pushed this war along. On the revolutionary side: Manuel Belgrano, founder of the Army of the North, who first raised the blue and white banner from a boat on the Paraná in February 1810, marched north into Upper Peru in May of the same year and won at San Luis and El Posta, only to be beaten at Vilcapugio in October 1813 and at Ayacucho in February 1814 until his corps was almost annihilated; José de San Martín, who worked the Andes from 1812, drilled fresh troops for the Army of the North, crossed the range in 1814 to retrieve the remnants of Ayacucho, and in 1814 to 1817 won at El Juncal, Chacabuco and Maipú in Chile, finally driving the royalists out of the far south of South America; Cornelio Saavedra, who presided over the Primera Junta that founded the state and yet asked in 1811 to have his own name struck from the minutes; Juan del Carril and Mariano Moreno, who argued for rewriting colonial law on the basis of popular sovereignty, and whose ideas shaped the 1813 statutes and the independence declaration of the Congress of Tucumán; José Gervasio Artigas, who organised the League of the Free Peoples in the Banda Oriental and made himself protector of it, forcing the centralists of Buenos Aires to give ground again and again, until Rivera beat his faction at the Battle of Flores in 1817 and Artigas withdrew into Paraguay; and Juan Lavalle, Martín Rodríguez and Vicente López y Planes, who in turn headed the government and drove the war to the limit of what the high road could bear. On the royalist side: Viceroy Hidalgo de Cisneros, who hurried back to Spain in May 1810; Gaspar de Vigodet, commander of the Royal Army, who fell back to Montevideo and fought Artigas and the Dragoons of San Marcos in the Banda Oriental; Pedro Anselmo de la Fuente, Rafael de Maroto, José Manuel de Goyeneche, Antonio de Quintanilla and Francisco Javier de Elío, who between them directed the defence of Upper Peru, Chile and Montevideo; and José de la Cánovas, who handed Lima over to San Martín in 1818. Most of the leading figures on both sides appear in the record as executors of establishment and of orders; the men who actually changed the war were the few who decided on withdrawal, on cutting the enemy apart, and on joining up. One episode in the Army of the North deserves recording: on 28 February 1814 the Seventh Line Infantry Regiment refused to advance on villages of its own kinsmen at Rodeo de Chací and simply dissolved on the spot, and since that criollo-dominated regiment was the backbone of the army, the act amounted to a declaration that the revolutionaries' own war had lost its object. Carlos María de Alvear became executive director in 1813 and fell in 1815 over his monarchical leanings and the mutiny of the troops, which shows that the revolutionary camp was permanently split between the republican and the monarchical road. Juan Lavalle moved the government to the eastern bank of the Uruguay in 1815, in effect abandoning Buenos Aires; Artigas withdrew into Paraguay in 1819 and died there in 1820.
kits: 卡面上這件火繩槍，是一五二〇年前後西班牙方陣步兵的制式槍：槍身一米五上下，槍口下方掛著點火的火繩，機匣裡盛著火硝，射手須先俯身讓火繩靠近火硝點著，再舉槍瞄準。這種槍在十八世紀末已被燧發槍取代，到一八一〇年的西屬南美只剩兩個位置：一是克里奧羅民兵的傢伙，獵人用的火繩獵槍沿用舊式，市面散槍價廉量足，卻難成排槍；二是在沒有彈藥、沒有火硝、沒有匠人的邊地當最後底子。民兵作戰時把火繩槍同長槍、獵槍、馬刀混編，槍手排成鬆散隊形，靠距離、地形與突襲取勝，而不是靠線列火力。相對地，王軍線列步兵早已改用燧發槍（西班牙陸軍在一八〇二年式定裝的燧發槍為標準制式槍），加裝刺刀，成排射擊與白刃衝鋒都強過火繩槍；安第斯軍在翻越山脈後改裝獵槍、繳獲的西班牙火器與土製火槍，只配少量燧發槍，槍械來源一半靠軍械庫、一半靠繳獲與私運。火炮方面，北方軍團以六磅至八磅野戰砲為骨幹，安第斯軍靠騾子分批馱運小型砲與十二磅砲翻山；騎兵是拉普拉塔流域真正的重裝力量，北方軍團有民兵騎兵與騎槍隊，安第斯軍有以聖馬丁騎兵為核心的槍騎兵團，隊員以長槍為主要兵器——這種「以騎槍對火繩槍」的搭配，是南美戰場上最耐用的組合。運輸依靠騾、馬、牛車與驛站線，海路則靠河口的小型武裝船隊與走私商船；補給是牛肉、馬黛茶、鹽與火藥，火藥多靠走私自巴西方向輸入。一八〇二年的西班牙軍令正式廢除長槍兵，線列步兵自此純以燧發槍與刺刀作戰；正因如此，革命軍民兵在方陣裡同時混用長矛、獵槍、火繩槍與馬刀，排槍時不齊、射程不一，卻勝在不必裝填齊射也能靠人多逼近。火藥的來路同樣值得一提：市售火藥價高量少，革命軍相當一部分火藥經巴西與英國方向走私上岸；一八〇六至一八〇七年繳獲的英軍槍械與火砲（數目以百計）則補足軍械庫的不足。河防方面，拉普拉塔與烏拉圭河上的武裝艇、河口的小型炮艇，以及在班達奧里恩泰爾鄉間往來的獵兵，構成了游擊戰的火力骨架。
kitsEn: The matchlock musket on the card was the standard arm of the Spanish square infantry around 1520: roughly a metre and a half long, with a slow match cord hanging from the lock, a pan charged with priming powder, and a shooter who had to stoop, bring the cord down to the pan to light it, and only then raise the piece to take aim. By the end of the eighteenth century the matchlock had been overtaken by the flintlock, and by 1810 in Spanish South America it kept only two places. The first was as the weapon of the criollo militia: hunters' matchlock guns followed the old pattern, and offcuts were cheap and plentiful on the market, though they could never be formed into volleys. The second was as the last resort in frontier districts where there was no ammunition, no powder and no armourer. Militiamen armed their matchlocks together with pikes, hunting guns and sabres, and shot in loose order, winning by distance, by ground and by ambush rather than by line fire. By contrast the royalist line infantry had long since taken the flintlock musket — the 1802 pattern flintlock was the standard arm of the Spanish army — and added the bayonet, giving them both disciplined volley fire and the shock of the charge, in both respects ahead of the matchlock. After the crossing of the Andes, San Martín's men armed themselves with hunting guns, captured Spanish pieces and country-made muskets, with only a sprinkling of flintlocks; the weapons came half from the depots and half from capture and smuggling. On the artillery side the Army of the North was built around six- and eight-pounder field guns, while the Army of the Andes moved its light pieces and twelve-pounders over the range in separate mule trains. Cavalry was the real shock force of the Río de la Plata: the Army of the North had mounted militia and lance troops, and the Army of the Andes a lancer regiment with San Martín's own riders at its core, the lance being their principal arm — that pairing of lance against matchlock proved the most durable on South American battlefields. Transport depended on mules, horses, ox carts and the post road, and at sea on small armed flotillas and smuggling craft in the estuary; the commissariat ran on beef, yerba mate, salt and powder, with the powder smuggled in mostly from Brazil. The 1802 Spanish regulations formally abolished the pikeman, and the line infantry fought from then on with flintlock and bayonet alone; it is precisely for that reason that the revolutionary militia used pikes, hunting guns, matchlocks and sabres in the same square — their volleys were ragged and their ranges unequal, but they could press home on numbers without any need for disciplined volley fire. The source of the powder deserves a mention as well: bought powder was dear and scarce, and a good part of the revolutionary powder was run ashore through Brazil and from the British direction, while Spanish cannon and small arms captured in 1806 and 1807, counted in hundreds, made up the shortfall in the depots. On the river, the armed boats of the Río de la Plata and the Uruguay, the little gunboats in the estuary and the hunters who moved about the countryside of the Banda Oriental formed the gunpowder skeleton of the guerrilla war.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術史，基本是兩個技術體系的對撞。王軍沿用十八世紀末以後的西班牙縱隊攻勢戰術：步兵以密集縱隊行軍，在接觸前展開成橫線，兩面射擊驅散對手，再以刺刀衝鋒突破，最後由騎兵追擊與擴張戰果；關鍵在於保持縱隊的秩序與速度，以及側翼與後方的火砲支援。這一整套在歐洲已被普魯士與法國人改良過的東西，落到安第斯山就整個崩了——山徑窄、騡子慢、缺草料，縱隊被拉成長蛇，飢餓、壞血病與高山夜寒在海拔兩千公尺以上大量殺傷非戰鬥減員。北方軍團的教訓最慘：一八一三年上秘魯戰役，貝爾格拉諾的民兵依舊以稀疏散兵線前進，士氣崩潰時不肯或不能對王軍的刺刀方陣發起衝鋒，屢次在對方的刺刀牆前停住，最後被王軍反衝與騎兵包抄碾碎。安第斯軍之後在智利卻改用縱隊快速通過狹隘地帶，把力量集中在少數幾個點上打有把握的會戰，邁普一役即是把縱隊集中於聖地亞哥城南的平坦地帶，先以砲火與騎兵威脅王軍側翼，再令步兵與砲兵在正面同時發動。民兵與游擊戰術在東方和南方卻行之有效：阿蒂加斯的利奇帕騎兵用馬刀、長矛與散槍打一場流動的鄉野戰爭，靠突然襲擊與游走破壞王軍的糧道與通訊；河口的小型武裝船隊攔截駛入蒙得維的亞的西班牙補給船，使維戈德特的守軍在市區裡挨餓；一八一六年之後聖馬丁把安第斯軍主力東調，以海路繞過王軍正面，迫使利瑪的西班牙當局在沒有援兵的狀況下必須議和。幾次關鍵的敗仗都出自同一個毛病：行軍線拉得太長。一八一四年二月北方軍團在上秘魯的雪原上連續行軍，隊伍被拉成數十里的散線，糧秣無法集中，火繩槍與獵槍在這種隊形裡根本談不上齊射；一八一五年拉瓦列北上重蹈同一覆轍，直到聖馬丁把戰爭重心南移、以海路與安第斯山天險換取時間，戰局才真正翻轉。
tacticsEn: The tactical history of this war is essentially a collision between two systems. The royalist army followed the Spanish doctrine of the attack by column as it stood at the end of the eighteenth century: the infantry marched in dense columns, deployed into a line on contact, shot from both flanks to unhinge the enemy, then drove forward with the bayonet, with the cavalry pursuing and widening the gap. What mattered was the order and speed of the column and the artillery support from the flanks and the rear. That whole apparatus, by then improved in Europe by Prussia and France, simply fell apart in the Andes: the tracks were narrow, the mules slow, the fodder scarce, the column stretched into a snake, and hunger, scurvy and the cold of the high nights killed enormous numbers of non-combatants above two thousand metres. The Army of the North paid the dearest price for it. In the Upper Peru campaign of 1813, Belgrano's militia still advanced in thin, loose lines; when their nerve broke they could not or would not charge the royalist square, halted again and again before the wall of bayonets, and were finally crushed by the counter-charge and by cavalry closing around them. The Army of the Andes then did the opposite in Chile, passing through the narrow defiles in columns, concentrating on a few points and fighting only battles it could win. At Maipú that meant concentrating the column on the open ground south of Santiago, threatening the royalist flank with artillery and cavalry first, and then bringing infantry and guns onto the front at the same moment. Militia and guerrilla methods, by contrast, worked well in the east and the south: Artigas's Charrúa horsemen fought a fluid country war with sabres, long spears and scatter guns, breaking the royalist supply lines and communications by sudden attack and by constant movement; small armed vessels in the estuary intercepted Spanish supply ships bound for Montevideo and starved Vigodet's garrison inside the city; and after 1816 San Martín shifted the main body of the Army of the Andes eastward, went by sea around the royalist front, and left the Spanish authorities in Lima to negotiate with no reinforcements on the way. Several of the decisive defeats came out of one and the same fault: the line of march stretched too far. In February 1814 the Army of the North was strung out in a scatter of tens of kilometres across the snows of Upper Peru, the commissariat could not be concentrated, and matchlocks and hunting guns in such a formation had no chance of a true volley; Lavalle's northern offensive of 1815 repeated the mistake, and only when San Martín shifted the centre of gravity south, buying time with the sea and the passes of the Andes, did the war genuinely turn.
data: 有根據可查的數字並不多，以下幾項是各方記載較常引用者。一八一〇年五月二十五日五月廣場公開議會的出席人群，多數記載為數千人規模，議會當日即以公投形式宣布市議會職權中止、臨時執政機關成立。王黨背後的海外壓力數字最為龐大：一八〇六至一八〇七年的英軍入侵拉普拉塔河口中，英軍在布宜諾斯艾利斯與蒙得維的亞兩役共死傷、被俘約一萬人上下（一說死約一千二百人、被俘約八千人），蒙得維的亞投降時英方留下的火砲與槍械數以百計，一說為一百二十門砲與近一萬九千支火槍；這些槍械後來成為革命軍的重要補充，也說明火繩槍一類舊式火器在美洲的存量遠比想像中大。北方軍團常態兵力多在兩千人上下，多為未受完整訓練的民兵；一八一四年二月阿亞庫喬一役出戰者約三千七百人，是整場戰爭中規模最大的一支出戰隊伍，卻在大雪與斷糧中全線潰敗，戰後僅約一千五百人隨聖馬丁北撤。安第斯軍最常被引用的規模是約三千三百人，配十餘門砲，騾馬數千，於一八一四年一月至二月間用十八日越過安第斯山，其中非戰鬥減員逾千人，各書數字有出入。邁普一役，愛國軍出戰約五千人，王軍約二千人上下（一說三千人），數字互有出入，但差距的方向一致。編制方面，一八一〇年布宜諾斯艾利斯民兵被整編為數個志願步兵團；砲兵方面，北方軍團與安第斯軍各自持有的火砲都在十門至二十門之間。戰爭全程歷八年零兩個月，戰場橫跨南美南部、秘魯高原與智利中部。另有兩個制度性的數字：國民代表大會自一八一三年一月在布宜諾斯艾利斯開議，至一八一六年七月在圖庫曼通過獨立宣言，前後三年；安第斯軍自一八一七年由聖地亞哥出兵，至一八一八年四月打成邁普會戰，其間橫跨的智利戰線長逾三百公里。
dataEn: Few hard numbers survive, and the following are the ones most often cited. The open cabildo in the Plaza de Mayo on 25 May 1810 is generally described as attended by several thousand people, and the cabildo voted the same day to suspend the municipal council and create a temporary governing authority. The largest figures belong to the overseas pressure on the royalists: in the British invasions of the Río de la Plata in 1806 and 1807 the British lost and left behind altogether of the order of ten thousand men at the two actions against Buenos Aires and Montevideo (one account gives some 1,200 dead and some 8,000 prisoners); when Montevideo capitulated the British left behind cannon and small arms counted in hundreds, one account giving a hundred and twenty guns and close on nineteen thousand muskets. Those arms later fed the revolutionary forces, and they also show how large a stock of older matchlock-era weapons really was in the Americas. The peacetime strength of the Army of the North was of the order of two thousand men, mostly militia without full training; the force that fought at Ayacucho in February 1814 numbered about thirty-seven hundred, the largest body ever put in the field in this war, and it collapsed completely in snow and hunger, only some fifteen hundred escaping north with San Martín. The most commonly quoted figures for the Army of the Andes are around thirty-three hundred men with a dozen or more guns and several thousand mules and horses, crossing the Andes in eighteen days between January and February 1814, with more than a thousand lost to sickness and exposure; the sources differ. At Maipú the patriot army engaged with about five thousand men against roughly two thousand royalists (some say three thousand); the figures vary, but the direction of the gap does not. In organisation terms the Buenos Aires militia of 1810 was reorganised into several volunteer infantry regiments, and in artillery the Army of the North and the Army of the Andes each held between ten and twenty guns. The war ran for eight years and two months, across the southern cone of South America, the Peruvian highlands and central Chile. Two institutional figures are worth recording: the Congress of the United Provinces first sat in Buenos Aires in January 1813 and passed the declaration of independence at Tucumán in July 1816, three years in all; and the Army of the Andes set out from Santiago in 1817 and fought at Maipú in April 1818, crossing a Chilean front of more than three hundred kilometres.
cause: 一八一〇年的布宜諾斯艾利斯並非突然革命，而是十年間不斷累積的危機總爆發。首先是英國入侵：一八〇六至一八〇七年英軍兩度沿拉普拉塔河溯流而上，攻陷布宜諾斯艾利斯與蒙得維的亞又撤走，暴露了總督府無力防衛王土的實況；此後總督希德諾斯入城第一件事就是改組市政並武裝市民，反而令克里奧羅知識份子與商人加深了對「土生人治理」的期待。其次是貿易的壅塞：塞維利亞壟斷制度限制本地船隻只能停靠蒙得維的亞，省際關卡又向克里奧羅商人徵收重稅，煙草、馬黛茶與皮革的專賣讓中間商與鄉紳怨聲載道；一八〇九年由商會主導的五月革命雖告失敗，卻說明土生精英已有組織，缺的只是一個成功的機會。第三是西班牙本土的崩解：斐迪南七世於一八〇八年退位後，一八一二年的加的斯制憲議會頒布憲法並接管美洲的效忠，克里奧羅人多認為自己同樣有權以公議會方式自治，於是省級的五月執政委員會在一八一〇年五月到六月間接連成立。第四是戰爭帶來的間接壓力：西屬美洲的金銀流向歐洲，航運封鎖與英軍封鎖削弱了布宜諾斯艾利斯的財政，港城商人要求開放自由貿易的呼聲越來越高。種種壓力交疊之下，五月二十五日由市政廳公告引發的一場群眾集會，變成了永久改變南美政治地圖的第一步。還有一層背景常被忽略：一八〇八年拿破崙廢黜波旁王室後，安達盧西亞與加的斯一線先後出現民眾組成的執政機關，一八〇九年西班牙王室在英國協助下復辟，克里奧羅知識份子由此得到一個明確的推論——母國既然已經用公議會推翻自己的君主，殖民地便有理由照做。
causeEn: Buenos Aires in 1810 did not revolt out of nowhere; the revolution was the sum total of a decade of accumulating crises. First, the British: in 1806 and 1807 the British came twice up the Río de la Plata, took Buenos Aires and Montevideo, and then withdrew, laying bare the fact that the viceregal government could not defend its own territory. What the viceroy Hidalgo de Cisneros did on arriving was to reorganise the municipal government and arm the citizens, and that only deepened the expectation among criollo intellectuals and merchants that the criollos themselves should govern. Second, commercial strangulation: the Seville monopoly confined local shipping to Montevideo, provincial customs duties weighed on criollo traders, and the state monopolies on tobacco, yerba mate and leather left middlemen and rural notables full of grievance; the open cabildo of May 1809, led by the consulado of merchants, failed, but it showed that the criollo elite could already organise and only lacked the right moment. Third, the collapse of metropolitan Spain: after Ferdinand VII's abdication in 1808 the constituent assembly at Cádiz promulgated a constitution in 1812 and took the allegiance of the Americas into its own hands, and many criollos argued that they too had a right to govern themselves through an open cabildo; provincial juntas of May and June 1810 followed one another across the provinces. Fourth, the indirect pressure of the European war: American silver and gold drained towards Europe, blockades and the British blockade thinned the revenues of Buenos Aires, and the port merchants' demand for free trade grew louder. With all these pressures crossing, a public meeting set off by a notice from the cabildo on 25 May became the first step in a permanent redrawing of South America's political map. One layer of the background is often overlooked: after Napoleon deposed the Bourbon monarchy in 1808, popular governing boards appeared in Andalusia and Cádiz, and in 1809 the Spanish monarchy was restored with British assistance, so that criollo intellectuals drew an obvious inference — if the mother country had already used an open assembly to dethrone its own sovereign, the colony had the same right.
impact: 這場戰爭最大的結果不是當年打贏的那幾仗，而是把維克托王國變成「聯合省」，同時把這個新國家的邊界、憲制與內部矛盾留給了後世。制度層面：一八一三年在布宜諾斯艾利斯召開的國民代表大會通過《一八一三年法典》，宣布奴隸制度廢除、給予奴隸制下出生者自由，確立了各省的自治框架；一八一六年圖庫曼議會的獨立宣言宣告「聯合省」為自由、主權獨立的國家；一八二六年布宜諾斯艾利斯制定第一部國家憲法，把中央集權的嘗試推到頂點後又崩潰，聯邦制與各省主權的問題一直懸到十九世紀末。地理層面：戰爭留下的最大未決問題是班達奧里恩泰爾的歸屬。阿蒂加斯的聯盟一度把勢力推過烏拉圭河，卻在一八一七年內部分裂，巴西出兵西屬班達奧里恩泰爾使蒙得維的亞重歸西班牙手中，一八一八年才隨革命軍收復；此後布宜諾斯艾利斯與巴西為這塊地方再起衝突，一八二五至一八二八年打了西普拉蒂那戰爭，輸掉的地塊成為後來烏拉圭的基礎，而一八二六年憲法曾把福克蘭（馬維納斯）群島列入國土，英國一八三三年佔領之後，爭議延續至今。區域層面：安第斯軍的南征把獨立浪潮從南美南端推向秘魯、玻利維亞、哥倫比亞與委內瑞拉，帝國崩解的連鎖反應自此不再受拉普拉塔的邊界限制。另一層長遠影響是國家的形狀：一八一四至一八一六年間中央政府事實上退到烏拉圭河東岸，首都與政府都曾離開布宜諾斯艾利斯，這段流亡期令省級勢力坐大，也令往後十年的政爭一直在「中央集權」與「聯邦」之間擺盪，軍人干政的傳統亦始於此。
impactEn: The greatest result of this war was not the battles won at the time but the conversion of the viceregal kingdom into the United Provinces, and the transmission to later generations of the new state's borders, its constitutional questions and its internal contradictions. At the institutional level: the Congress of the United Provinces, sitting in Buenos Aires in 1813, passed the Statutes of the Year XIII, abolishing slavery, granting freedom to those born under it and setting out a framework of provincial autonomy; the declaration of independence read at Tucumán in 1816 proclaimed the United Provinces a free and sovereign nation; and the first national constitution, drafted in Buenos Aires in 1826, pushed the experiment in centralisation to its limit and then broke, leaving the question of federalism and provincial sovereignty unsettled until the end of the nineteenth century. At the geographical level the war's greatest unfinished business was the fate of the Banda Oriental. Artigas's league at one point carried its power across the Uruguay, but it split internally in 1817, a Brazilian invasion of the Spanish Banda Oriental returned Montevideo to royalist hands, and the city was only retaken by the revolutionary forces in 1818. The quarrel between Buenos Aires and Brazil over that territory followed, producing the Cisplatine War of 1825 to 1828, whose lost territory became the basis of later Uruguay; and since the 1826 constitution listed the Falkland (Malvinas) islands among the national domain, the British occupation of 1833 opened a dispute that is still unresolved. At the regional level: the southward march of the Army of the Andes pushed the tide of independence from the far south of South America towards Peru, Bolivia, Colombia and Venezuela, and the chain reaction of imperial collapse was no longer confined by the boundaries of the Río de la Plata. Another long-term effect was the shape of the state: between 1814 and 1816 the central government was in fact pushed back to the eastern bank of the Uruguay, and both the capital and the government left Buenos Aires for a time. That exile in the provinces let the provincial powers grow, and the struggles of the following decade swung between centralisation and federation, with the tradition of soldiers in politics beginning here.
result: 結果可以分三層講。軍事上：一八一〇年五月被推翻的西班牙維克托總督府再未能在拉普拉塔河口恢復統治；希德諾斯返西班牙，繼任者由塞維利亞三人執政政府任命，最末一任總督何塞·德·拉·塞爾納於一八一四年到任、一八一六年被俘後押往西班牙，拉普拉塔省總督的名號正式消失。一八一八年春，聖馬丁把安第斯軍自智利調回，越過安第斯東麓山脈直取利瑪，七月二十八日在利瑪市政廳宣布秘魯獨立，戰爭以這一日畫上句號，阿根廷獨立戰爭通常以此為終點。與此同時，阿蒂加斯的聯盟在內戰式的衝突中瓦解：一八一四年《聖托托梅條約》之後布宜諾斯艾利斯與利奇帕聯邦對抗，一八一七年里維拉在「弗洛雷斯戰役」擊敗阿蒂加斯派系，阿蒂加斯退入巴拉圭，省分的中央集權化與聯邦的崩解同時開始。政治上：聯合省在一八一六年獲得國際法意義上的獨立，克里奧羅菁英從次級臣民變成國家建造者，主權議會、憲法與常備軍的骨架在戰時匆忙搭起，也把軍方干政、地方割據與外國干預的病根留給下一代。國際上：安第斯軍的南征把西屬美洲的崩解時鐘撥快，秘魯、玻利維亞、哥倫比亞、委內瑞拉與墨西哥在往後十二年間相繼脫離馬德里，最後由玻利維亞的亞亞庫喬與秘魯的胡寧兩役決定性地終結南美王室軍的命運。戰爭的直接結果亦有一項常被略去：王黨在拉普拉塔河口最堅固的堡壘蒙得維的亞，直到一八一八年才隨革命軍的推進而陷落，守軍總司令維戈德特棄城離去；同年之後，整個南美南部再沒有一支成建制的西班牙王室軍。
resultEn: The outcome can be read on three levels. Militarily: the Spanish viceregal government overthrown in May 1810 never recovered its rule at the mouth of the Río de la Plata. Cisneros went back to Spain; his successors were appointed by the Seville triumvirate; the last viceroy, José de la Serna, arrived in 1814 and was carried off to Spain as a prisoner in 1816, and with him the name of the viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata disappeared. In the spring of 1818 San Martín brought the Army of the Andes back from Chile, crossed the eastern foothills of the Andes and struck directly at Lima; on 28 July the city hall of Lima saw Peru's independence proclaimed, and that is the day on which the war is normally closed, and with it the Argentine War of Independence. At the same time Artigas's league was broken apart in a civil war of its own: after the Treaty of Santo Tomé of 1814 Buenos Aires and the Federal League fought it out, Rivera beat Artigas's faction at the Battle of Flores in 1817, Artigas withdrew into Paraguay, and the centralisation of the provinces and the dissolution of the federation began together. Politically: the United Provinces obtained independence in the international legal sense in 1816, the criollo elite changed from second-rank subjects into builders of a state, and the skeleton of a sovereign congress, a constitution and a standing army was hastily put together in wartime — along with the seeds of military intervention in politics, local caudillismo and foreign meddling, handed down to the next generation. Internationally: the southward march of the Army of the Andes turned the clock of Spanish American collapse forward, and Peru, Bolivia, Colombia, Venezuela and Mexico left Madrid one after another over the following twelve years, the royal armies of South America finally being ended at Ayacucho in Bolivia in 1824 and at Junín in Peru in the same year. One direct result is often passed over: the strongest royalist fortress in the estuary, Montevideo, did not fall to the revolutionary armies until 1818, and its governor Vigodet abandoned the city in flight; after that year there was no organised royal army left anywhere in the southern cone of South America.
